type: A tight sans with strong contrast and a single accent.

goals.audience: Software founders and sellers (owners of vertical software companies), and investors — large private-equity firms and sovereign wealth funds. Secondary audiences: customers of Fullsteam's vertical software companies, and employees/candidates. Primary lens: investors, founders secondary.
goals.action: Explore our vertical solutions, then take the next step and start a conversation with Fullsteam (Contact). The site is a credibility/validation destination, not a lead-gen funnel — its core job is helping a warm visitor understand who Fullsteam is before a meeting.
goals.success: A founder or investor leaves understanding Fullsteam's scale and its two-part model — we acquire and grow vertical software companies, and we grow them through Embedded Offerings (payments, lending, insurance, AI) — and reaches out. Success is measured by exploration depth and credibility, not form fills.

brand.assets: We have a logo and some guidance

voiceLine: Whatever the industry, we own the software it runs on. A permanent home for each software business we buy — plus the Offerings that help it grow.

inspiration.love: Quilt Software (quiltsoftware.com) — brand consistency, a premium feel, prominent company stats, and strong use of video (mission video + customer video testimonials). Bending Spoons (bendingspoons.com) — a unique, engaging experience with a premium product feel on the homepage. Square (squareup.com) — overall look and feel and a seamless way of introducing broad verticals. TogetherWork (togetherwork.com) — clean look and feel; introducing verticals directly on the homepage without a page per industry. DaySmart (daysmart.com) — how they showcase the product portfolio and talk about mission and values. Frontier Growth (frontiergrowth.com) — use of video (including hero video) and well-structured homepage content blocks (not their font). Investor-brand feel: silverlake.com and thomabravo.com. AI presentation: banyansoftware.com/ai-at-banyan and ecisolutions.com/ai-strategy.
inspiration.avoid: Stock photography; dated typography and look & feel (the Frontier Growth font); talking-head-only video and "word walls"; an over-GTM, product-led portfolio framing (DaySmart); framing an acquisition as an "exit" (it's "a home for your business"); the label "Platform" (use "Embedded Offerings"); publishing revenue, run-rate, or explicit profitability; floating/scattered vertical "bubbles"; and PPC/lead-gen funnels.
